| | | | | | Friend,
Today, former Las Cruces Mayor Ken Miyagishima announced that he is ending his campaign for Governor and joining ours.
In announcing his endorsement, Ken shared:
_**“I realized that the best way to make a difference in New Mexico is by teaming up with my good friend, and former Mayor Gregg Hull.”**_
Ken and I did not enter this race from the same political party. We served different cities in different parts of our state. Yet as mayors, we faced many of the same challenges, and we learned that potholes are not Republican or Democratic, public safety is not a partisan issue, and creating good jobs should never take a back seat to political games.
We both know what it means to lead a city, balance a budget, work with people from every background, and be held accountable for real results.
That is why Ken’s endorsement matters.
This campaign is becoming a place where New Mexicans can come together around something bigger than party labels: safer communities, a stronger economy, better schools, responsible leadership, and a state government that works for the people it serves.
Ken could have stepped away from this race quietly. Instead, he chose to stand with us and help build the coalition needed to win in November.
**Now I am asking you to stand with us too.**
Our opponent will have millions of dollars and a national fundraising network behind her. We are building something different: a New Mexico campaign powered by people ready to move our state in a new direction.
**Will you contribute $25, $50, $100, or another amount today to help us share this endorsement across New Mexico and reach the voters who will decide this election?**
---

| | This is more than one endorsement. It is proof that New Mexicans are ready to move beyond the same old divisions and choose leadership grounded in experience, cooperation, and results.
Ken and I are joining forces. With your help, we will bring New Mexico together and win.
Thank you,

This is my opponent Scott Desjarlais. Just a month ago, after unspeakable damage to our communities, he **celebrated** funding ICE... and insisted it's for the safety of Americans.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4659ce35-4bba-428a-a3f0-3871c8de2df7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But let's be clear here, George Washington was a British subject born in colonial America. Alexander Hamilton was born in the Caribbean. Thomas Paine came from England. James Wilson came from Scotland. Long before the United States even existed, the people who shaped it were people who crossed oceans, built new lives, and helped define what this country would become.
**In other words, the word** _**immigrant**_**has been part of the American story since the very beginning, and funding breaking down that community isn 't some fix-all.**
**[I'm fighting for leadership that focuses on people, not division, and would be honored to have your help today.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN TO HOMETOWNS OVER HEADLINES!!️](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lately, though, you'd think the word "immigrant" itself was some kind of insult. It isn't. An immigrant is simply someone who comes to a new country. Throughout American history those people have built farms, cities, railroads, schools, businesses, and communities. They've served in our military, cared for our neighbors, started companies, and raised families that are just as American as anyone else.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fcca5395-7dd6-4bcb-abe4-4be47b06684a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### The word immigrant isn't a cuss word. It's part of the American story.
When politicians reduce complicated history to a single soundbite, it shrinks the conversation instead of expanding it. America wasn't built by one group of people or one generation. It was built by pioneers, workers, farmers, builders, dreamers, and yes, immigrants too. That has always been the reality of this country, whether some people want to admit it or not.
I'm not running to inflame debates or score viral moments online. This campaign exists because communities need leaders who actually show up, listen, and focus on the real challenges families are facing every day. Keeping our families safe, supporting struggling small businesses, helping families trying to get ahead, and aid parents working to give their kids better opportunities than they had.
If you want leadership focused on communities instead of outrage, help us keep moving forward. **[Even a small contribution helps us keep spreading a message grounded in reality and respect for the people who make this country work.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE $15 !](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Because at the end of the day, America's strength has never come from dividing people into categories. It has come from people showing up, working hard, and building something bigger together. **That 's the future I'm fighting for.**

body:
| Friends, I wanted to reach out to you personally about the state of our race.

[There are a lot of pieces moving, and things are changing by the second, so if you’re still with me, I’m hoping I can count on your $7 split between me and Voter Protection Project to flip this seat blue. »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/119125?t=6&akid=26606%2E878179%2E7OL6lq) | [Before you read any further, please rush a donation to help me flip South Carolina blue »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/119125?t=7&akid=26606%2E878179%2E7OL6lq)
---
What’s happening in the Palmetto State is truly unprecedented. There hasn't been an open Senate seat in 23 years.

Back in 2003, when I was still in med school and flared jeans were all the rage, South Carolina *actually* had a Democratic Senator.

And that’s what we’re aiming for again in 2026 – a Democratic Senator to fight for all of you. **But let me be clear: our campaign just entered a brand-new, uncharted phase.**

While we don’t know our opponent yet, what we do know is whoever they are, they're starting at $0, which means Republicans are chomping at the bit to pour as much money as possible into keeping this seat red.

That’s why when I tell you we haven’t faced a more critical moment in this entire campaign, I mean it.

[If you are with me and believe that South Carolina is ready for true change, I’m hoping I can count on you to help me raise $500,000 in the next 24 hours by chipping in $7 right now split between me and Voter Protection Project. » ](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/119125?t=8&akid=26606%2E878179%2E7OL6lq)

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1879, the notorious gunslinger and dentist [Doc Holliday killed a man](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAURb_GbEa2YzAMHrqwpWtH5OBHeOkDR_ZLEH9fUfUPOp-rq3vP13W8BiTc7p9hBc9zGjfYCwEz5PFVOKf0LN9IBLEkShE33O5hNMq0Ujmp-zEGpGO0VfQzgIFLBV67ztqmcaatFt-F3jrbmhDVfLMzuBigU6D7qMMEqqnQn23K6V4r1dm2blpz06DVNDk9WdUKqyAip1w_Em68wExHekOup7RW5BfmZxGXD2EGYYZ93-sFC6d8nFyYgRcsMoZD4ib_iDDD40WH1L0wQ0yTXBIRnpnzapFzypIXkDPmwpJxhSr7-NyRCEvrhFX3NSD9DuB_WXt78xMAAP__SRWDdw) for the first time after the man shot up his saloon in New Mexico. This marked one of his only eight confirmed shootouts, despite his formidable reputation. If you watched _Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom_ on Sunday evenings in the 1960s, you experienced the very beginning of television's wildlife and nature genre. The brand continues today with both spinoffs and original episodes, as we see in today's [_Whatever Happened To ..._](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVvQnWNsGDx0QRmarpW6IMAHXHvBEXaCePsqfYXOv_QN_-e1u_YsvM4f_Y18nmK30p6Ecqate6S8xXhPPyxCIUWJgVde577ToO0J3AmbLvQsR2eK4CciTeeCPLramKpy2haL7wHJDgbpPAxTgAqRJsCmNk1NFRIW7F8aOGwQoDa2rKwekBDG0eFowCoDFDjHrfyOvOaFJjnik7ZyjLdC_JLzPanzm9Kt0u2-7-URH_kx0Ksr3aYlbjkp3V7my8zy_jW5VGw-3HcW4WSdMjDfepY_L_9rwtPr3wAAAP__O9Fw7A) section. In case you missed it, this week on _The Flyover Podcast_ , Ayla tackled the phone battery problem that has almost nothing to do with your actual battery. It turns out a handful of settings are running in the background all day, quietly draining power without you ever touching them, and shutting them off costs you nothing. From the toggles most people never think to check to the ones switched on the day the phone left the box, Ayla walked through seven quick fixes that can stretch a single charge well past what you are getting now. [See tips here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzz1OwzAUAODTOFuj5_9k8ICEspWRslmp_dw8cOMqdltyewRX4AKf9J2O_jhTpvXyNl_RtVT8is-asTXc_L22rZRb_aKcMdaSS6SV1svsBQhzAHvgo48z5d2rLrqEKFB26LgdlNLaCtMtTiVMo0lmECGIGIIelR4HJS2PAGfkHblfDSwfOcCgTK-NOHPkEILlQYFhCjBSK1v_WWhtC6a8lwdufSjXLrultVtl8oWJiYlpL_d278_IxLS8nx7f-oMfF2Byaky-Sim7zcXbk3KmaixTcLnOlP-k9q_-w4mfAAAA___xp2z5)! ## Two US Soldiers Killed, One Missing
Two U.S. service members [were killed in Jordan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuhDAURL8GOiPbvEzhIg3dpk2JjH2Bu_Fj5etdtH8fkXxC2hlpNOd83ZabQY9x_zQBdNnSEuEkD6VAXp5UckoP-kbvwVHyyWHEuJtFcjkwPjIxLc6gfy9d7fQGIKGtQYtRdV3fj3KoDy16xd0ohdpavgJfwU7tZLixk12nDVSN-lrjo5gE56obmn6QqwDBrR2F7fhQdRwclpSbe8JYDtj8O70gNzaF2uujlAdV7Ucl50rO53k2cbUXxdVfScreVXIO6JwHBoZKJedyJvYkRpBfaIEFCCtkYn-o7J6yM5GZmMoBmQUkwrgzC7GkwMi8iWUbTa-UUKLO2j1O9B5pGKuO78Gg_z1X_mX0peVPAAAA__87X42m) on Friday while defending against Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks, and a third remains missing, U.S. Central Command announced Saturday. Four others were briefly hospitalized and have since been discharged. The strikes follow [a broader wave](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAURp8Gb1hA8N_A0MVbuna0sLnYt8FgwXWs9Omr9BU6f9Knc87XfbpbDBjXT7uDIZ-mCFcJQAR5OgvllI7ywBDAlRSSw4hxtZMSquWi43KYnMXwmnTljAdQcKvAyK7Xumk61VabEfPsZiUHOTRNN4jWq8U3DVin-2GQoq_QvN9EJwcpRK_bumnVLEGKZenkokXLtACHlHL9nTDSBj680hNyvaS9CmYjOgq7fTA1MjVe11Uvc3lbvHemxoBP4OfhLEFhasRsI79s5pTP_eCFskXiyfMt5f384ZbILo_CD8gFbeTrGTxTY5WNOy4MAUvbMS3W3WL4I6B_ZXsa9RsAAP__RF6DoA) of Iranian attacks targeting U.S. allies Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain in recent days. Iran's supreme leader warned of ["unforgettable lessons"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdF6ZwQu8gmKjiO5FkVKkRAaPdycZPMg2oP37iPzCq490dc_5_Tl9OmKKzx9uxaEEmSKembEUTNOeSxLZ8l9iRp-FxVOk-HQTGGi16XT9MXlH_J5s5YeACNhUONRdb-393kFbvQaLLfTB9rObDVgXPBgMs-0NNFjPTVvRcK2Zrv6ojelte7u3MNdYm2Xp6sWaVlmDnoqk2x-hWF4Y-C0Hptsia8XDq5Qtq-ahYFQwnud5W3O8mIIRo96zgvGSuqAk9gpGSi7qvG8JV9SMzmPSbln2jFmXtK-blqAPEnaF4lN7dKwPObMOkhYMO-uEeZOYUcHokn48oJ_Hn0U1oyzkVfP925UUz_wL01alwW8nMVNuO2XNc3XE_8-XLxU_BvgXAAD__9FmmCA) if American strikes continue, and Tehran suspended its commitments to the interim deal signed last month to end the fighting.
## Trump Threatens Tariffs over Smoke

**Whatever happened to _Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom_?** For millions of Americans, Sunday nights meant a folksy zoologist in a khaki shirt saying, _"Welcome to Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom."_ [Here's one of the show's openings](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwVssvgz2wBCpStUhWTsiDJf4tgRcQ2Ll7av0FbqeI_2G_-fZnh0mzNeLu4FpsdgMe03QGmz2XttWylq_MSUItaQSMGO-OsspVweqD2yywWF6WtkFEwE4iA4M06OUw6C56hajwyhjEKMfZhe4F4OLkU18ckpKxoB1aF4a1WxilI5S9YPiMwNGvdfMS6qIpBCwla3_KpjbAjE9ywO23pdbl8zS2lqJOBJ-Ivy073v_LPd2n-H1vxbX_ELE6UHE2_vlOB9Xesk_H91mwrpjSliVJpJebw7TH9n-1eFh-G8AAAD__2qtcVY). The show didn't just fill an hour before the workweek--it invented an entire genre, hauling anacondas and lions into living rooms decades before _Animal Planet_ or _Shark Week_ existed. So where did it go? It never really left. _Wild Kingdom_ debuted on NBC on January 6, 1963, hosted by Marlin Perkins--a University of Missouri zoology dropout. At its peak, the show drew an average of 34 million viewers, powered by [Perkins' scholarly manner and the derring-do of his younger sidekick, Jim Fowler](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVvQnWNsGDx0QRmarpW6IMAHXHvBEXaCePsqfYXOv_QN_-e1u_YsvM4f_Y18nmK30p6Ecqate6S8xXhPPyxCIUWJgVde577ToO0J3AmbLvQsR2eK4CciTeeCPLramKpy2haL7wHJDgbpPAxTgAqRJsCmNk1NFRIW7F8aOGwQoDa2rKwekBDG0eFowCoDFDjHrfyOvOaFJjnik7ZyjLdC_JLzPanzm9Kt0u2-7-URH_kx0Ksr3aYlbjkp3V7my8zy_jW5VGw-3HcW4WSdMjDfepY_L_9rwtPr3wAAAP__O9Fw7A), who tended to do the actual snake-wrestling while Marlin narrated from a safe distance. This fueled a running gag Johnny Carson loved during their many _Tonight Show_ visits, which became a highlight on Carson's show. [Here's a clip with Fowler, Carson, and a coyote from 1969.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAUheGnwVusC8bgDAyVqrRLMlSqqkwIw3V8E2Iig2Pl7Sv3FbqeI33D_3O0R0eRpsvJ3dGUIdkJ1xyxFJztksuc0iPfKEYMOcUUaKLp4qwAoXagd3xvg6P4srIKZkAU2FRouO6kbFstVDWaHhvetwrbxg8QvIZ2LzoVpO6UGKCDisymgeZ7DtBJVbdK9Bw5eK-5l6CYBAxU0lxfE01lxCG-0hPn2qd7Fc1YyiOz5o2JAxOHdV3rV1rK0uP2b4srfmTN4cma9-PXefk-fVzPn7dqNuGxUoyUlWYSLndH8Y8s_-rwNOI3AAD__woEcQo) But Perkins came by his caution honestly. Back in 1928, as a young reptile curator at the St. Louis Zoo, he was bitten on the finger by a Gaboon viper--one of Africa's deadliest snakes--with no antivenom on hand. He survived, becoming one of only a handful of people ever known to do so. The show ran new episodes from 1963 to 1971, then continued in syndication. In 1985, Perkins stepped down as host to fight lymph cancer; he died at home in St. Louis in June 1986 at age 81. The brand proved durable. _Animal Planet_ revived it in 2002 with Alec Baldwin narrating, and a newer incarnation, _Protecting the Wild_ , is co-hosted by Peter Gros and Dr. Rae Wynn-Grant. Classic Perkins-era episodes [still air Sunday mornings on the nostalgia-oriented MeTV](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQxvGnMVvQ-TA2DB4qtdnSNd2QsY9wrcERdoLy9hV9ha7fJ_2G__UyXBxHXm-fbiFbpjSstOdIpdA2PHLZUrrnH46RQk4xBV55vbkBAfUJzEn2Q3AcX4Oqgp2IkJqKrDSdUm1rUFezbcYOwjS2jiRKEyD0gKgN9k7rrpe6YntoYGQvATql61bjKEmC90Z6BVoooMAlbfV34rXMNMVXetJW-7RU0c6l3LNo3gSeBZ73fa9f6VEeIx3_sbjiZ9Gcn6J59_qrX7K7GvVRbTbcd46RszZCwW1xHP_I8q8OT4u_AQAA__-5YHB5), serving many of the same viewers who grew up on the show. _Were you a fan of Wild Kingdom? For millions of Americans, Sunday nights meant a folksy zoologist in a khaki shirt saying, "Welcome to Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom." . The show didn't just fill an hour before the workweek--it invented an entire genre, hauling anacondas and lions into living rooms decades before Animal Planet or Shark Week existed. So where did it go? It never really left. Wild Kingdom debuted on NBC on January 6, 1963, hosted by Marlin Perkins--a University of Missouri zoology dropout. At its peak, the show drew an average of 34 million viewers, powered by , who tended to do the actual snake-wrestling while Marlin narrated from a safe distance. This fueled a running gag Johnny Carson loved during their many Tonight Show visits, which became a highlight on Carson's show. But Perkins came by his caution honestly. Back in 1928, as a young reptile curator at the St. Louis Zoo, he was bitten on the finger by a Gaboon viper--one of Africa's deadliest snakes--with no antivenom on hand. He survived, becoming one of only a handful of people ever known to do so. The show ran new episodes from 1963 to 1971, then continued in syndication. In 1985, Perkins stepped down as host to fight lymph cancer; he died at home in St. Louis in June 1986 at age 81. The brand proved durable. Animal Planet revived it in 2002 with Alec Baldwin narrating, and a newer incarnation, Protecting the Wild , is co-hosted by Peter Gros and Dr. Rae Wynn-Grant. The declaration would unlock federal money to rebuild homes and infrastructure. [State crews rescued more than 270 people](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ywyAQhU-DOjSwwkYUFGnUOW1KDRKLRIKMB9aWffuMnCOkfm--9_N1GS8upnhdPt2Glp4hj1fca0IiLKObpkxUEX8qlft2c9EfKs4jCDhzobk0o3cxvUbVeDsJb2SDVupeqVNvlG5Wq32nTNC6dxBOJ4OTgj7MSneTAAWITbQHTGhppBQAqu1mCK7THoVxPUjJlEAfKZeWViR8uhrSKz-wtHPemmRXoltl3QeDgcGw73sb8hPOa75XytfDxGA4ejMYNvedC_exukpYuMc5uYKev7E8pJx95UvBhf9tb4r1tz2mFOtZMyWWzcX0zqX_vfWw8BsAAP__YZ-BGg), and local teams near Uvalde about 300 more.
